title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta filo pastry pie
excerpt: The great Greek filo pie: layers of buttered, papery filo surrounding a filling of spinach, feta, dill, and egg, baked until shatteringly crisp and golden. Eaten warm or at room temperature, equally good for lunch or as a starter.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spanakopita (spinach pie) is one of the most beloved dishes of Greek cuisine and is found across the country in various forms: as a large tin pie cut into squares, as individual triangles or rolls, or as a coiled spiral. Filo pastry (from the Greek word for leaf) is the essential element; its multiple layers, each brushed with olive oil or butter, create the characteristic shattering crispness. The filling varies by region and family but always contains spinach and feta; eggs bind the filling and dill is the standard herb. Squeezing the spinach completely dry is the most important technique: any moisture left in the spinach will steam inside the pastry, making the filo soggy and preventing it from crisping properly.

content.text: Squeeze the cooked spinach in a clean tea towel until completely dry; it will reduce dramatically and lose more water than seems possible. Wet spinach is the most common cause of soggy spanakopita. Keep the filo sheets covered with a damp tea towel while you work; they dry out and crack within minutes of exposure to air.

items.preparation: fresh; or 500g frozen spinach defrosted; wilted and squeezed completely dry
finely diced and softened in a little oil

content.text: Heat the oven to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas 5. Mix the squeezed dry spinach with 300 g crumbled feta, beaten eggs, softened onion, spring onion, dill, nutmeg, and pepper. Taste and add salt only if needed (feta is very salty).

Brush a 30 x 22 cm baking tin with melted butter. Layer 8 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each generously with butter. Spread the filling evenly. Layer 8 more sheets of filo on top, each brushed with butter. Tuck any overhanging edges in. Score the top layers into squares or diamonds without cutting through to the filling.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and very crisp. Leave to cool for 10 minutes before cutting along the scored lines. Serve warm or at room temperature.
